direction.name: The pinned poster
direction.idea: Something stays put while everything else changes. A title holds its place across the viewport and the images beneath it swap; the name is split to two opposite corners and the page passes between the halves; a single frame stays centred while its contents change. Every scroll step is a new cover of the same magazine. The idea suits subjects that are a series (a book of portraits, a line-up, a collection, a set of projects): the fixed element says what the series is, the changing element shows its members.
direction.composition: A sticky layer holds the fixed element for the height of two to three viewports: usually the title at 10–14vw across the middle or top of the screen, or two words pinned to the top-left and bottom-right corners. Under it, a stack of full-height panels scrolls by, each a single large photograph (portrait 4:5, centred, 40–50% of the viewport wide) with one line of caption at the same small size everywhere. The title sits above the images in the stacking order and uses `mix-blend-mode: difference` or a solid colour that reads on every panel. When the pinned run ends, the page releases into ordinary flowing sections with a narrow measure. Build with `position: sticky`; never hijack the scroll.
direction.typography: The pinned title is the only large type on the page. Captions and body share one small size (15–17px). Tight tracking and solid weight so the title reads over photographs.
direction.colour: One strong title colour against a pale or dark ground. Each panel may take its own flat ground colour sampled from its photograph.
direction.imagery: A series of photographs with the same crop ratio and the same framing (all portraits, all objects, all rooms), so that swapping them reads as one image changing. Five to eight in the pinned run.
direction.richness: Repetition with change. The fixed title makes each new photograph feel like an event, so the photographs must be good and consistent.
direction.pitfalls: If the title is not legible over every panel, the idea fails: test each one. Keep the pinned run under six viewports or it feels like a trap. On a phone the title shrinks to 16–18vw and stays pinned at the top; panels become full-width. A pin longer than three screens, or one where the screens under it are nearly empty, read in blind tests as a stuck page. Every screen under the pin needs its own content, and nothing may pass over the pinned words.

hero.name: Name split to corners
hero.blueprint: The name is cut into two halves that stay pinned to opposite corners while the page passes between them. A layer with `position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh` and `pointer-events: none` holds both: the first word top-left, 28px from the top and left edges; the second word bottom-right, 28px from the bottom and right edges. Both are set at clamp(72px, 9vw, 140px), line-height 0.85, in white with `mix-blend-mode: difference` so they read on every panel beneath. On the first screen the stage between them is a paper-white panel on columns 1–9 and one full-height photograph on columns 10–12 touching the top, right and bottom edges. The supporting sentence, 20px and max 34ch, starts at column 3 at 44% of the height; the single action is a text link with an arrow directly under it. Three text links are stacked at 15px along the right edge of the white panel at mid-height. The rest of the panel is empty. Later panels, full-height photographs and text panels of different widths, scroll under the pinned halves for three to five viewports; then the layer releases into ordinary sections.
hero.mobile: Both halves stay pinned: the first word top-left and the second bottom-right, each at 15vw with 16px margins. Between them every panel is a full-width photograph 56svh tall followed by its sentence at 17px. On the first screen the photograph crosses the middle band with the supporting sentence and the action link beneath it. The stacked links collapse to one word at the top-right corner.
hero.headline: The name in two halves (two words, or one word cut at a syllable), each up to about 9 characters at 9vw, one per corner, with no other headline.

type.note: A heavy sans with tight joins and an eccentric lowercase, friendly but loud. Suits bookshops, food, consumer subscriptions and marketing studios.

palette.name: Charcoal and sage
palette.note: Charcoal holds the page with off-white text, and one section may flip to a pale concrete tone with dark text. Colour comes from the photographs; grey sage is used for the single button and the active state of a control.

motion.name: Pinned story
motion.description: One element holds its place with `position: sticky` (a title, a frame, a product fragment) while the items that belong to it scroll past or swap inside it. The page's ordinary scrolling does the work; nothing is hijacked. Keep the pinned run under six screens. Recipe: 'Pinned story' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Pinned sentence, photographs pass
sections.blueprint: A wrapper 300svh tall. Inside it a `position: sticky; top: 0` layer of 100svh holds one sentence of 8–14 words, centred, three lines at clamp(36px, 4.6vw, 68px), leading 1.1, in a block 62% of the viewport wide. The sentence is a paragraph, not a heading; it is white with `mix-blend-mode: difference` (or a solid ink that reads over every photograph) and has a higher `z-index` than the images. Behind it, three photographs sit in normal flow at different sizes and sides and scroll past the fixed sentence: a 4:5 portrait 24vw wide with its left edge at 6vw; 70svh lower a 16:10 landscape 38vw wide touching the right margin; 70svh lower a 1:1 frame 18vw wide starting at 30vw. Each crosses the sentence once. When the wrapper ends, the sentence releases and scrolls away with the last photograph. No scroll hijacking.
sections.mobile: Wrapper 260svh. The sentence pins at 40% of the screen height at 8.4vw, four or five lines, with 20px margins. Photographs alternate: 64% wide on the left margin, 78% wide on the right margin, then 52% on the left, with 50svh between them.

sections.name: Line-up at one type size
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed flat section. The programme is a four-column table spanning the full width between 24px margins, with every cell at one size, clamp(20px, 2.1vw, 30px), one weight, no bold: the act or session flush left, the format starting at 33%, the room or stage at 66%, and the time range right-aligned at the far edge with tabular figures. Rows are 1.5em tall and separated by nothing but that leading; the fixed column starts do the organising. Day or part headings are a single line at the same size in the accent ink with 72px above and 20px below, and may be `position: sticky; top: 0` on a strip of the section's ground colour so the current day stays in view. Breaks and changeovers are rows set in capitals in the soft ink. There is no other heading. Comfortably holds 12–40 rows; with fewer than eight, raise the size to 3vw.
sections.mobile: Each entry becomes two lines: the act at 22px on the first, then format, room and time on one line at 14px in the soft ink with the time right-aligned. 18px between entries. Day headings stay sticky at the top on the ground colour.

sections.name: Close-up with column card
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed close-up photograph, 100vw by 100svh, with nothing over most of it. A four-column grid lies on top. One solid card in the ink colour, exactly one grid column wide (about 22vw) and 52svh tall, sits in the second column, vertically centred. Inside it, centred: the item's name at 30–36px, a variant line at 17px, the price or key fact at 17px, a small 3:2 photograph of the whole object (the card shows the whole, the background shows the detail), and at the foot a square-cornered action filling the card's width. The card is opaque, radius 0–6px, with no blur. When the section presents two or three items, each gets its own full-bleed frame and its card moves one column to the right each time, so position carries the sequence. The first card's name is the section heading.
sections.mobile: The photograph fills 100svh, cropped to its most detailed area. The card becomes a full-width block docked to the bottom, 46svh tall, left-aligned inside with 20px padding; the small whole-object photograph sits to the right of the name at 96px wide.

sections.name: One frame, contents change
sections.blueprint: Instead of many pictures side by side, one frame stays in place and its contents change. The frame is small and exact: 300px square on a quiet page, or up to 40vw at 4:5 on an object-led one, centred or sitting on the text column's left edge, with at least 20vh of empty ground above and below. Five to seven photographs are stacked inside it with `position: absolute` and crossfade in turn (opacity over 600ms, each held for 2.4 seconds, via CSS keyframes with staggered delays). All are shot or cropped alike: same scale, same light direction, the subject at the same position, so only the subject seems to change. On a flat ground use `mix-blend-mode: multiply` so studio backgrounds vanish. One caption line at 14px sits 16px below the frame and changes with the image. No arrows and no counter. On a motif-led page the frame takes the motif's shape through `clip-path`.
sections.mobile: The frame is 72vw wide, centred, in a section 70svh tall. The crossfade continues on its own; tapping the frame advances to the next image at once. The caption sits beneath, centred, at 14px. When reduced motion is requested the first image holds and tapping still advances.

sections.name: Last photograph, text beside
sections.blueprint: A final full-bleed photograph, 100vw by 90svh, chosen so its subject sits in the left half and its right half is calm. All text is confined to the right half and never crosses the centre line: in columns 8–12, anchored to the lower third, a closing line of three to five words at about 3.4vw in a light weight, a paragraph of two or three lines at 17px, and one filled button in the paper colour with ink text, about 52px tall. If the image behind the text is not calm enough, darken the whole photograph slightly with `filter: brightness(0.8)` rather than laying a panel behind the words. The section butts directly against a footer in one solid colour, so the photograph's bottom edge is a hard line. No logo, no second action.
sections.mobile: The photograph is 100vw by 70svh, cropped to keep its subject. The text leaves the image and sits beneath it on the footer's solid colour: closing line at 28px, paragraph at 17px, full-width button. Image and colour meet at a hard edge.

sections.name: Name first, places under it
sections.blueprint: The wordmark opens the footer instead of closing it. On a full-bleed field in the page's inverse or final chapter colour, the name spans the full content width as the first thing, its cap line pushed 8% above the footer's top edge so the tops of the letters are sliced off by the section (`overflow: hidden` and a negative top margin in `em`). 72px beneath, a two-part row: columns 1–5 list the places or ways to reach the studio (cities, or email and telephone), one per line at 32–36px in the accent ink, each a link; columns 7–12 hold three columns of small links at 15px, top-aligned with the first place. A final row 96px lower carries the legal line at the left and a back-to-top text link at the right, both 13px. The field is about 90svh tall, and nothing sits between the wordmark and the row but space.
sections.mobile: The sliced wordmark stays at the top, fitted to the width. Places follow as a list at 26px, then the link columns two across at 15px. Legal line and back-to-top link share the last row at 12px, at opposite margins.

references.name: City of Angels
references.idea: A fixed poster: the book title stays pinned across the viewport while portraits and press quotes swap underneath it, so every scroll step is a new cover.
references.hero: Pale icy-blue page. The title runs as one line of extra-bold uppercase grotesk at 10vw, centred, spanning about 82% of the width in saturated cyan, 120px from the top. A single portrait photograph, 37% of the viewport wide and nearly full height, is centred beneath; the title crosses over its upper quarter, so the middle letters sit on the image. The author name sits top-centre in small bold caps, a two-bar menu icon top-right. Bottom-left, a 13-line bold paragraph in a narrow 340px column; bottom-right, a solid black five-point star about 70px wide.
references.type: ABC Diatype throughout: weight 800 uppercase for the 144px title, bold copy around 20-24px with leading near 1.0; Founders Grotesk Mono in tiny caps for quote attributions. Two sizes plus a label. The final frame catches title letters slanting to oblique.
references.colour: #e4f8fd #06aeef #0a0a0a #c8b59d — The page colour is a pale tint of the title's cyan; cyan appears only on the title, the opening words and quotation marks. Text and star are black. The digest records one solid cyan section.
references.imagery: Full-length street-style portraits, all vertical at about 2:3, saturated natural light, subject standing centre. One image at a time, square corners, centred on the page with the title overprinting it.
references.layout: One pinned composition repeated for seven screens: central image column, fixed title, and a single text block that alternates between the left and right gutters and shifts height each step. Margins about 46px; nothing else on screen.

sections.description: Each scroll step keeps the pinned title and swaps the central portrait. One press quote sits in a column 180-340px wide in an outer gutter, alternating right, left, right, and placed at a different height each time (upper, middle, lower). Quotes are bold black with tight leading and cyan quotation marks; the source follows in tiny underlined or mono caps. The black star stays bottom-right and is caught at different rotation angles.

Not captured in the shots, but the digest records four stacked, centred, uppercase links at 144px (10vw) in the same extra-bold grotesk, plus a solid cyan section: navigation reuses the title's exact type size, one link per line, so the menu is another poster rather than a small list.

steal: Pin one giant title across the viewport and let a single centred image change beneath it, with the type overprinting the photo's top quarter.
Use a pale tint of the accent colour as the page background so the saturated title and the background read as one hue.
Give each scroll step one text block and move it between left and right gutters at varying heights instead of stacking sections.

references.name: Revelatio Studio
references.idea: The team photograph is the hero: it starts as a small CRT-curved mosaic of typographic glyphs and resolves into a full-bleed group portrait as you scroll.
references.hero: Pure black viewport. Centred, about 58% of the width and 57% of the height, is a canvas showing a group photo rebuilt from tiny coloured glyphs, its edges barrel-distorted like a CRT tube; it is dim, so black dominates. The headline is modest: two lines at 2.5vw in regular-weight grotesk, flush to the bottom-left corner with a 30px margin. Navigation is split into two small dark-grey rounded rectangles: logo mark plus four links top-left, language switch and contact top-right. Nothing else; roughly 80% of the screen is black.
references.type: Neue Haas Grotesk Text 55 Roman is the only face and weight. Headline just 36px with -0.03em tracking against 15px body; hierarchy comes from position and grey value. The footer city list jumps to roughly 5vw; the digest records a 12.5vw maximum.
references.colour: #000000 #ffffff #2b2b2b #8a8a8a — Black intro and footer, white work and capabilities sections. The interface has no accent; all colour comes from project thumbnails and the faint tints inside the glyph mosaic.
references.imagery: A studio group portrait rendered as a glyph mosaic on canvas, then as a dim near-full-bleed photograph; project tiles are square-cornered brand visuals in saturated flat colours, set on white with caption rows beneath.
references.layout: About 30px side margins throughout. Black full-screen opening, then a white work grid mixing one large tile with a narrow companion and a three-up row, a three-column plain-text capabilities list, and a black footer of oversized dim text. Captions sit under images, tags right-aligned.

sections.description: Pinned for about two viewports: the hero canvas grows with scroll from a centred 58%-wide mosaic to a near full-bleed image with a thin black margin, while the glyph cells shrink until the picture reads as a dim photograph of about twenty people. The headline scrolls away and only the two nav boxes remain in the top corners.

White background. First row: one large landscape tile spanning roughly two-thirds of the width beside a narrower tile about one-third wide and half as tall, top-aligned. Second row: three equal tiles. All square-cornered with about 16px gutters. Beneath each: project name at left, two tiny grey tags right-aligned on the same line, then a two-line grey description at about 11px. A small underlined see-all link with an arrow sits below the grid at left.

White section opened by a hairline and a tiny label. Three text columns, each with a small grey category title and beneath it a tight stack of eight to ten service names in 15px regular grotesk at about 1.2 line-height, with no bullets, icons or cards. Columns share the work grid's left edges, leaving the right third partly empty.

Black full-viewport block filled with a run-on, comma-separated list of client cities set at about 5vw in very dark grey, barely visible against black, wrapping over seven flush-left lines. Exactly one city, the last, is lit white, which implies a cycling highlight. The nav boxes stay fixed at the top corners.

steal: Render a photograph as a grid of small coloured glyphs on canvas and let scroll increase its size and resolution until it becomes the real photo.
Hold the hero headline at 2.5vw in a bottom corner and let a dim central image and empty black carry the scale.
Set a long list in near-invisible dark grey at display size and light one item at a time.

references.name: Kereliott
references.idea: A quiet house gets a quiet page: one dark field, one typeface, the name set as wide as the screen and photographs left to drift in generous darkness.
references.hero: Very dark green-black field with cream type. A two-line introductory sentence at about 30px sits top-left inside 30px margins; a small cream rectangular button sits top-right. The upper half is otherwise empty. The house name fills the full content width in a flared humanist sans, mixed case, with capitals about 19vw tall, its baseline at roughly 87% of the viewport height. Immediately beneath, separated by a gap of a few pixels, the top sliver of a full-width landscape photograph enters from the bottom edge.
references.type: A single face, Trust, in regular weight: a humanist sans with flared terminals and old-style figures. The wordmark is an oversized graphic; all other text is one size of about 20-30px plus tiny 10px photo captions. Hierarchy is position, not weight.
references.colour: #161c1a #eae8dc #222926 #1f2926 — Cream on green-black from top to bottom with no accent colour. The map is drawn in a tone barely lighter than the ground, so photographs supply all the colour.
references.imagery: Natural-light photos of a stone cottage, garden and deck with square corners, in mixed portrait and landscape crops at differing sizes. One full-width opener, then small images placed singly with tiny captions under the left corner.
references.layout: 30px margins, text held to the left 60% in one size. Photographs are staggered left and right at different widths with large dark gaps between, like pictures passed on a wall. The name and a booking button stay fixed in the top corners.

sections.description: A full-width landscape photograph runs margin to margin directly under the wordmark, followed after a gap by a four-line paragraph in the single text size, left-aligned and spanning about 85% of the width. There is no heading or label; the text simply continues the sentence begun at the top of the page.

After a left-aligned paragraph, a silhouette map of the region sits centre-left, about half the viewport wide, filled in a green only a few percent lighter than the background. Five towns are marked with small ring dots and tiny labels; only the house's town has a solid cream dot. No border, legend or frame.

Photographs are placed one or two per screen in a stagger: a portrait image about 30% wide against the left margin, a larger near-square one starting lower against the right margin, later a landscape image top-right of centre and a smaller one bottom-left. Each has a 10px caption under its left corner. More than half of every screen is empty dark ground.

Two short left-aligned sentences in the standard text size with underlined inline links to booking platforms and an email address, then a small cream certification badge. The footer is a single line at the very bottom: social link left, copyright centre, three underlined utility links right, with a tall empty gap above.

steal: Size the wordmark to fill the content width exactly and let the first photograph tuck directly under its baseline.
Draw a location map as a tone-on-tone silhouette with one filled dot among ring dots.
Use a single typeface in one weight and essentially one text size, creating hierarchy through placement and emptiness.
